newsitem.title: UK: UK natgas quieter, demand falls on warmer weather.
newsitem.headline: UK natgas quieter, demand falls on warmer weather.

text.p: The UK spot gas market saw much quieter trade on Thursday than on recent days, traders and brokers said, with dealers describing the underlying sentiment as softer although prices were little moved.

"It's a combination of the election, warmer weather and people taking stock," said a trader, accounting for the quiet market. Another agreed, saying that administrative tasks relating to the end of the month had kept him from trading at all.
The short term market was once again relatively active, with trade seen for within the day and the day ahead as well as combinations of days in early March and the whole of the balance of the month.

Prices were slightly softer, with day ahead gas traded at 10.70 pence at the NBP, compared with trade at 10.80 and 10.90 pence on Wednesday. This reflected the warm weather on Thursday and a projection for even warmer weather on Friday.

Further out little change was seen. The period May 6 to 31 traded at 10.60 pence on Thursday; exactly the same level was seen for the period May 2-31 the day before. June was done at 10.575, down fractionally from 10.60 pence on Wednesday, and both Q3 and Q4 were slightly softer, although dealers said they had traded at the low end of existing ranges rather than moving into a new, lower range.

One trader who sold significant volumes on Thursday said the warmer weather had not had a great influence on prices. "There are quite a few buyers, so it's possible to shift some at reasonable prices, but there's not much difference caused by the weather," he said.

The summer months were weaker on IPE futures, where July, August and September all traded down by up to 0.13 pence a therm. But there was an unexpected price increase seen further out, with both March and April 1998 coming up, March by 0.16 pence a therm. But trade was also relatively quiet on futures, with 115 lots traded in 10 deals.

The warm weather is set to continue and push demand down even further. Transco said that Friday's temperature is forecast at 15.9 Celsius, up from Thursday's 15.8 Celsius and compared with a seasonal normal level of 11.5 Celsius. As a result demand will fall even further, to an estimated 151 mcm or 35 percent of peak day demand, the lowest of the year so far.
